news.title: Infantino under pressure to include abandoned World Cup sell-off plan in external Fifa review
news.lede: Council members also want Balogun affair included. Fifa president says review letter been well received. Fifa council members will demand that Gianni Infantino include the abandoned World Cup sell-off plan and the Folarin Balogun affair in his proposed external review of Fifa’s governance. In a letter sent to all 211 of Fifa’s member associations on Monday, Infantino said he would ask the council to commission a review of “Fifa’s current governance framework for major strategic initiatives” at its next meeting, in Zurich on 15 October, but he faces an internal battle over its terms of reference.

news.title: Harry Kane tipped to play at next World Cup weeks before he turns 37 by England boss Thomas Tuchel
news.lede: HARRY KANE has been tipped by England boss Thomas Tuchel to star at the next World Cup — weeks before he turns 37. The veteran Three Lions captain faces Spain in the Nations League on Saturday night. And Tuchel said: “No problem, age is just age, it doesn’t matter. “It is only about quality — and he still has a long way to go.”

news.title: Virgil van Dijk: Liverpool captain slams Dutch reporter following claims he forced Ronald Koeman to change World Cup tactics
news.lede: Virgil van Dijk hit back at suggestions that he forced former Netherlands boss Ronaldo Koeman into changing his tactics during the World Cup. The Liverpool defender captained his country during the tournament, where they were knocked out by Morocco on penalties in the round of 32. The 35-year-old has retained his captaincy under new boss Xavi, and was involved in a frosty confrontation with a journalist during a spiky press conference ahead of Netherlands' Nations League clash with Germany on Thursday. news.title: Moroccan officials selected for Qatar U-17 World Cup
news.lede: Moroccan refereeing has made a new mark on the global stage after FIFA announced the official list of referees who will officiate matches at the U-17 World Cup, scheduled to take place in Qatar. The list includes the names of two Moroccan referees: Mohamed Al-Baroudi, as the head referee, and Abdel Samad Aberton, as part of the assistant referee team, ensuring that Moroccan refereeing is represented in one of the world’s most prominent youth competitions. FIFA has selected 81 referees and refereeing officials to participate in the tournament, which Qatar will host from November 19 to December 13, 2026. The selection of Al-Baroudi and Aberton reinforces the presence of Moroccan referees in international competitions and underscores FIFA’s continued reliance on Moroccan refereeing expertise on the global stage.
